analysis.is_complaint_reason: The customer expresses dissatisfaction and reports a financial loss of £4,250 after being tricked into transferring savings to a fraudster. She wants the money back. Under CH-1 this is a complaint.
analysis.summary: Ms [PERSON_2], aged 78 and recently bereaved, received a text claiming to be from HMRC about a tax refund. She then got a call from someone posing as Harbourline security, who told her to move her savings to a 'safe account'. On 12/09 she sent £4,250 by Faster Payment to an account in the name of [PERSON_1]. She reported it on 2026-09-14. Her card was blocked and her credentials were reset. No fraud team referral was made, she had to chase on 2026-09-30, and there was still no owner on 2026-10-21. She has asked for large-print letters. The deadline status is Critical with 0 days left.

timeline.event: Customer received a text claiming to be from HMRC about a tax refund, then a call from someone claiming to be Harbourline security.
Customer transferred £4,250 by FPS at 14:32 to an account in the name of [PERSON_1].
Customer reported the scam by phone. Card blocked, online banking credentials reset, customer told the fraud team would be in touch.
Customer called chasing. No record of a fraud team referral. Customer asked for letters in large print.
Chased internally. Still no fraud team owner.

analysis.severity_reason: This is a suspected APP scam with a loss of £4,250 (over £1,000). The customer is elderly, bereaved and has low digital capability, so she is a vulnerable customer at risk of harm. The deadline is Critical.

vulnerability.suggested_support: Refer to Vulnerable Customer Support. Send all letters in large print as requested. Consider a named contact and more time to respond, and ask her sensitively about any other support needs. The health driver is flagged as possible only (age 78, very distressed), pending a conversation with her.

analysis.routing_reason: This is an APP scam, so it must go to Fraud & Scams under FRD-2 and ESC-1. The 1 business day handover deadline was missed by several weeks. The customer is vulnerable (bereavement, low digital capability) and there is a risk to her wellbeing, so a VUL-4 referral to Vulnerable Customer Support is needed. Senior Complaints Review is suggested, at the handler's discretion, because of the Critical deadline and the internal failure to refer. No ESC-1 trigger for that team is evidenced; it is a judgement call.
